misconception: A stable toy service has 12 people present on average and 3 arrivals/minute. What is the mean time in the system? The prediction alternatives contrast different consequences of the stated model.

claims.text: A stable toy service has 12 people present on average and 3 arrivals/minute. What is the mean time in the system? Options: 2 minutes; 4 minutes; 12 minutes. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.
claims.source: Stipulated numerical case in model.ts, based on manager numericCase: Stable flow with meanarrivalrate3/min and averagepeopleL=12 impliesmeanW4min. DoubleLto24withrate3 gives8min; doublebothL24andrate6 restores4min. Distinguish long-run law from per-customer promise.

claims.text: A stable system averages 18 items and 6 arrivals/hour. Mean time? 18/6=3 hours.
claims.source: Transfer arithmetic or model implication under the same explicitly stated assumptions. Independent verification pending.

claims.text: The retained cases show 4 and 8 minutes. The arrival rate is unchanged; doubling average occupancy doubles the corresponding average time.

claims.text: Little’s law is L=λW for a stable flow with consistent boundaries and long-run averages. It relates averages, not a promise that each customer waits exactly that long.
